title: The Championship Game

bio.Courage: You step up when things feel scary.
bio.Kindness: You notice when someone is hurting, and you help.
bio.Honesty: You tell the truth, even when it's hard.
bio.Curiosity: You look closely, and you try new things.
bio.Teamwork: You know that working together makes everyone stronger.
bio.Grit: You keep going, and you don't give up.

text: You are the fastest player on the Tigers soccer team, and the championship game is this Saturday!
At practice, there's a new kid named Sam. Sam keeps tripping over the ball, and some of the kids are laughing.
Coach Dee blows her whistle. "Free practice time!"

choices.t: Practice your own shooting, extra hard
choices.log: You worked hard on your shooting

choices.t: Tell the other kids to stop laughing

text: It's Saturday! The stands are full, and your family is cheering.
Right before halftime, you land funny and twist your ankle. It hurts. Not a lot, but it hurts.
The score is tied, one to one. Coach Dee calls out, "Everybody okay?"

choices.t: Tell Coach the truth about your ankle
choices.log: You told Coach about your ankle

text: One minute left. Still tied. You get the ball, and you race down the field.
A big defender is coming right at you. Out of the corner of your eye, you see Sam, wide open by the goal.
The crowd is yelling. It's time to decide!
The ball flies, and... GOAL! The Tigers win the championship!
Everyone runs onto the field. But near the goal, a girl from the other team named Priya is sitting on the grass, crying.
Your teammates are jumping and shouting. Nobody else notices Priya.

choices.t: Help Priya up and tell her "Great game"
Bring your whole team over to shake hands

endings.text: It was Sam who scored the winning goal! The new kid who kept tripping at practice. Sam ran straight to you and said, "I couldn't have done it without you."
Your shot curved right past the goalie. The crowd went wild!
Your brand-new move faked out the defender, and the ball rolled to Sam, who tapped it in. Nobody had ever seen a move like that!
That night, your ankle was swollen and sore. It meant two whole weeks of no soccer. Next time, telling Coach might be the smarter play.
Because you told Coach, the trainer wrapped your ankle at halftime, and it was ready for that big final minute.
After the game, Priya's coach found you. "That was real sportsmanship," she said. Priya waved goodbye with a small smile.
After the game, Priya's coach found you. "That was real sportsmanship," she said. Priya waved goodbye with a small smile.
On the way home, you looked back and saw Priya still sitting on the grass. Winning felt great. But you wondered how Priya felt.

talk: Sam was new and kept tripping. How do you think Sam felt when kids laughed?
Is it ever okay to hide when you're hurt so you can keep playing? Why or why not?
Priya's team lost. What could you say to someone who just lost a big game?
